src/application/CancelOrderUseCase.ts: order.cancel() hands the cancellation rule to the domain aggregate, so the use case does not decide on its own whether cancelling is allowed.
src/application/CancelOrderUseCase.ts: await this.stock.release(order.lines) and await this.orders.save(order) coordinate domain services and ports, which is application orchestration.
src/application/CancelOrderUseCase.ts: return toOrderDto(order) maps the result to an application DTO. It builds no HTTP response and sets no status codes.
src/application/CancelOrderUseCase.ts: the not-found guard throws DomainError("not_found", ...). This is a normal use-case precondition check, not transport logic.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: CancelOrderUseCase does only application-layer orchestration. It loads the aggregate through a domain repository port and handles the not-found case. The cancellation rule itself stays in the domain, through order.cancel(). The use case then coordinates stock release through a domain service, saves the aggregate through the port and maps the result to an application DTO. The file has no persistence code, no transport or HTTP handling and no framework logic. The use case does not reimplement any business rule inline. Every responsibility fits the application layer kind.
